svg.text: Everything inside the 300 x 200 x 130 box, lid off, seen from the front. Microphone and 4G antenna are internal; the Witty Pi 4 carries the DC/DC. Cable numbers match the schedule.
A Interior layout and cable routing
on a shelf above the battery
4 glands, all on the UNDERSIDE. The mic port is a 5 mm hole in the wall, not a gland.
the panel's own 80 cm leads, MC4 cut off, ferruled
2 x 2.5 mm2 + inline 15 A blade fuse + ring terminals
MPPT LOAD to Witty Pi 4 VIN
Witty Pi's supplied 30 cm XH2.54 lead, ferrules at the MPPT
GPIO header, no cable; the Witty Pi powers the Pi through it
5 V and GND from the USB-A breakout to both probe leads
own 2 m leads: A/B to the RS485 adapter, +/- to the breakout
6-core Dupont on I2S, via a stacking header under the Witty Pi
Gone since the first drawing: the buck and its cable, the terminal block, the MOSFET probe switch, the lavalier and sound
card, the antenna pigtail and whip, the 20 m cable and its junction box. Seven runs where there were thirteen.
The Witty Pi 4 takes 12 V from the LOAD output on its own 6 to 30 V input and
feeds the Pi through the GPIO header at up to 3 A. No buck, no USB power lead.
The probes take 5 V from a USB breakout, so they go on and off with the Pi.
Never wire them to the load output: it is not switched, and they would draw
0.5 W around the clock, more than the whole winter budget.
Witty Pi 4 uses GPIO 2, 3, 4 and 17 and watches GPIO 14. The I2S pins 18-21
are free; the mic needs a stacking header under the Witty Pi for room only.
Both probes leave the factory on Modbus address 1. Re-address one to 2
(register 07D0) on the bench, or they collide and neither reads.
SEN0600 exposes moisture (0000H) and temperature (0001H) only, so it uses
the sen0600 profile, which reads two registers rather than three.
Probe wire colours are not published. Meter them before splicing: the family
convention is brown +V, black GND, yellow A, blue B.
Leave the galvanised steel mounting plate out of the box. A 4G antenna radiates through the plastic wall for a few dB of loss, but a steel plate beside it detunes the antenna and
puts nulls in the pattern. Mount the boards on a cut sheet of 3 mm plastic instead. Paint the box: ABS is not UV-stable, and the paint is its protection before it is camouflage.
Nothing here is verified on hardware yet. Meter every colour and check every connector against the part in your hand before you cut anything.
